android.desc:
Stop pausing. Start understanding. Video Summarizer turns long YouTube videos into clear, structured summaries you can read in minutes.

WHY IT HELPS

Save time: get the key takeaways from long videos in minutes.

Make smarter decisions: uncover key arguments, pros and cons, and actionable insights.

Learn more: ask follow-up questions and explore topics in your preferred language with AI.

FEATURES

Summarize inside YouTube: summarize videos and comments, read results, and customize summaries without leaving the YouTube app.

Quick summaries: paste or share a video link to get a summary tailored to your needs.

In-depth insights: uncover key claims, evidence, pros and cons, and actionable takeaways.

Comment insights: discover common opinions, debates, useful tips, and frequently asked questions.

Flexible formats: choose quick bullet points, structured outlines, or detailed summaries in your preferred language.

AI chat: ask questions, clarify concepts, and explore ideas without rewatching the video.

Save & share: keep your summaries organized and share them with others or send them to your computer.

Backup & restore: back up your summaries and restore them when needed.

Made for professionals, creators, students, and curious minds. Learn faster, research smarter, and spend less time watching.

quotes.text:
Seems to use gpt-4o under the hood. I wonder if using Deepseek would make any difference in quality.

I used to have nice and detailed summaries with this app lasting many paragraphs. It used to be totally free and you could submit as many links as you wanted. However they started forcing you to wait dozens of hours between summaries or pay for credits. I haven't found a YouTube summarizer as high quality since.

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.emote.youtube_summarizer

I'm thinking one could replicate such a service pretty easily and be able to plug in your Deepseek API token instead. It would be convenient if such services let you "bring your own API key" so to speak, so you'd only have to manage one bank of credits. But it's understandable that lots of people want in on a slice of the AI pie right now.
quotes.story_title: TL;DW: Too Long; Didn't Watch Distill YouTube Videos to the Relevant Information
